Status, Stakeholders, and Flexibility

状态、相关方与灵活性

The Fallacy of Status状态报告的谬误

Udi Dahan · Haifa, IsraelUdi Dahan · 以色列海法

AFTER A SUCCESSFUL FIRST PROJECT, I confidently embarked on my second. This was a larger project, it was more strategic to my employer, and I would manage a multidisciplinary team of people. I was sure that the skills that had served me the first time around wouldn't fail. Interestingly enough, it was my trust in my team's status reports that was my eventual undoing. About two months into the project, my infrastructure team lead confessed, "It turns out some of the architectural assumptions we made were unfounded." However, he assured me that, "We'll be back on track by the end of the month." Despite his reassurances and the contingency buffers I had in place, I couldn't dismiss the sense that something was wrong. At the end of the month, I followed up with the same team lead. He showed me how the refactoring work had been completed on schedule and how the developers were all set to hit their targets for the coming month. When I sat down with my integration team lead, she notified me that everything looked good from her vantage point, too. Modules were complying with their specifications, each had been sufficiently tested, and all the multiple layers of the architecture tested stable enough for the first integration. After a slightly bumpy first integration (as many of them are) and a regular quality assurance cycle, I was astounded to discover that almost every use case had critical bugs in it. We were almost 5 months into the 15-month schedule, but nowhere near a third done with our project work.

第一个项目成功后，我自信地开始了第二个。这是一个更大的项目，对我的雇主更具战略意义，我要管理一个多学科团队。我确信第一次奏效的技能不会让我失望。有趣的是，最终让我栽跟头的，正是我对团队状态报告的信任。项目大约两个月时，我的基础设施团队负责人坦白说："原来我们做的一些架构假设是没有根据的。"但他向我保证："我们月底前会重回正轨。"尽管有他的保证和我设的应急缓冲，我还是挥之不去一种感觉：有什么不对。月底，我找同一个团队负责人跟进。他给我看重构工作如何按计划完成、开发如何都准备好达成下个月目标。当我和集成团队负责人坐下时，她也告诉我从她的视角看一切都好。模块符合规格，每个都经过充分测试，架构的多层都测试得足够稳定，可以做第一次集成。在一次略颠簸的首次集成（很多集成都这样）和常规 QA 周期后，我震惊地发现几乎每个用例都有关键 bug。我们在 15 个月进度里已过了近 5 个月，但项目工作远没做到三分之一。

— p.188 —

I remained certain that all the team members would pull together to finish on time. One month before we were supposed to be going live, everyone was reporting that their work was at least 95% done. However, when I brought in one of our real users to try the system out, she told me in no uncertain terms, "This is broken in so many ways, I couldn't stand working with anything like it." That didn't sound like a project 95% done to me. An experienced project manager, Patrick, was brought in to "save the day." While Patrick, the project savior, (and today, my mentor) was getting things back on track, he explained to me the fallacy of status. The customer defines "done," not a status report. The fact that the database team reported 95% completion had no real bearing on whether our users could use what we developed. Even if the status reports looked perfect, they were giving an incorrect view of the project progress. In short, the project was doomed, practically from day one, because I wasn't mapping to the goals of the project. I finally understood why I always needed to work with users to have them evaluate each feature as it was created, to be sure it added customer-perceived value. That way, the project status reports, converted to earned-value reports, show the true percentage of earned value created rather than only showing how much work is left.

我仍然确信所有团队成员会齐心协力按时完成。上线前一个月，每个人都报告自己的工作至少完成了 95%。然而，当我带来一位真实用户试用系统时，她毫不含糊地告诉我："这东西从那么多方面都是坏的，我受不了用这样的东西。"在我听来这不像一个完成 95% 的项目。一位有经验的项目经理 Patrick 被请来"救场"。当 Patrick（项目救星、今天我的导师）把事情拉回正轨时，他向我解释了状态报告的谬误。是客户定义"完成"，不是状态报告。数据库团队报告 95% 完成，对我们用户能否使用我们开发的东西没有真正影响。即使状态报告看起来完美，它们给出的项目进展视图也是错的。简言之，项目几乎从第一天起就注定失败，因为我没有映射到项目目标。我终于明白为什么我总是需要和用户一起工作，让他们在每个功能创建时就评估它，确保它增加了客户感知的价值。这样，项目状态报告转换成挣值报告后，显示的是已创造挣值的真实百分比，而不只是还剩多少工作。

— p.189 —

What Do They Want to Hear, Anyway?他们到底想听到什么？

Martha Legare, MBA, PMP · Atlanta, Georgia, U.S.Martha Legare（MBA, PMP）· 美国佐治亚州亚特兰大

PROJECT COMMUNICATION TAKES MANY FORMS—from "management by walking around" to formal presentations. I consider communication the most critical set of activities in a project. The hardest, yet the most common, way to convey software project information from one person to the next is a formal presentation. Some polls find that public speaking is more frightening than death or the dentist! Most presentations are too long, boring, and riddled with too much detail. Look at your last presentation and see if it could accurately be described as "death by PowerPoint." If your answer is "yes," you can redesign your next one so it truly communicates to your audience. Ask yourself, "What is the best mode of presentation for what I want to accomplish?" If you have a small group and want give-and-take discussions, using a flip chart or a whiteboard to capture areas of concern or agreement is a useful technique. However, if you want executives to approve a particular project or agree to a new project tact, a multimedia slideshow could work. The trick is to realize that regardless of the technology you employ, you are what sells the idea to your audience—not your slides, posters, or laser light shows. We must engage both left-brain logic and right-brain creativity in order to effectively sell our ideas. Use the statistical proof, but showcase it in a memorable format. Use easy-to-understand color charts and graphs, and just a few bullet points.

项目沟通有多种形式——从"走动式管理"到正式汇报。我把沟通视为项目中最关键的一组活动。把软件项目信息从一个人传到下一个人最难、却最常见的方式是正式汇报。有些民调发现公开演讲比死亡或看牙医还可怕！大多数汇报太长、无聊、充满太多细节。看看你上次的汇报，能不能准确描述为"PowerPoint 致死"。如果答案是"能"，你可以重新设计下一次，让它真正向听众传达。问自己："对我要达成的事，最佳汇报方式是什么？"如果是小群体、想有来有回地讨论，用翻纸板或白板记录关注或共识的地方是有用技巧。然而，如果你想让高管批准某个项目或同意新项目策略，多媒体幻灯片可能奏效。诀窍是意识到无论你用什么技术，把想法卖给听众的是你——不是你的幻灯片、海报或激光秀。我们必须同时调用左脑逻辑和右脑创造力，才能有效卖出想法。用统计证据，但以难忘的形式展示。用易懂的彩色图表，只用几条要点。

— p.190 —

Explain the story behind each bullet point, rather than using too much text and reading it aloud a beat after participants have already read it for themselves. Plan your presentation ahead of time using a whiteboard and sticky notes rather than starting directly with PowerPoint. Brainstorming on sticky notes allows you to see the big picture and easily rearrange ideas without feeling you are destroying hours of work. Place your sticky notes in "affinity" groups, combining similar concepts, and then think about how to craft those ideas into a meaningful and memorable story. Always come back to the questions "What's my central point?" and "Why does it matter to this specific audience?" Capture interest by creating curiosity or showing the unexpected, then use concrete illustrations to support your numbers with something your audience can visualize. For example, a Wall Street Journal article described an executive who lost enough of his company's money that if you took crisp $100 bills and stacked them on top of one another, they would reach the 92nd floor of his Madison Avenue office. That's a memorable image. When in doubt, delete all but the essentials. You can prepare a handout for people to read later if they want more detailed information, and a take-away document will ensure that your facts won't get distorted. This approach will guarantee that you will present your essentials succinctly. And when you find out that the president has cut your presentation from 30 minutes to 5 in order to make his golf tee-time, you'll be prepared to summarize on the spot.

解释每条要点背后的故事，而不是用太多文字、在参与者自己读完一拍后大声念出来。提前用白板和便利贴规划汇报，而不是直接打开 PowerPoint。在便利贴上头脑风暴让你看到大局、轻松重排想法，而不觉得在毁掉几小时工作。把便利贴按"亲和"分组，合并相似概念，然后思考如何把这些想法打造成一个有意义、难忘的故事。总是回到这两个问题："我的中心论点是什么？""为什么对这个特定听众重要？"通过制造好奇或展示意外来抓住兴趣，然后用具体图示给你的数字配上听众能想象的东西。例如，《华尔街日报》一篇文章描述一位高管亏了公司足够多的钱——如果你崭新百元钞一张叠一张，会堆到他麦迪逊大道办公室的 92 层。那是个难忘的画面。拿不准时，删掉除要点外的一切。你可以准备一份讲义供人之后想了解更详细信息时读，带走的文档会确保你的事实不被歪曲。这种方法保证你简洁地呈现要点。当你发现总裁为了赶高尔夫开球时间把你的汇报从 30 分钟砍到 5 分钟，你已准备好当场总结。

— p.191 —

Recognize the Value of Team Morale认识团队士气的价值

David Bock · Reston, Virginia, U.S.David Bock · 美国弗吉尼亚州雷斯顿

MORALE IS ONE OF THOSE THINGS YOU KNOW YOU NEED, but it is hard to grow and measure. A team with high morale will occasionally put in extra effort cheerfully, but a team with low morale will not. High morale isn't just about a better workplace, it is about a more productive team. A few years ago, I worked with a team that exhibited high morale. At times, the office felt more like a community of friends than a workplace. Productivity was high. We would occasionally have crises that required a little extra "push," and team members would volunteer for that extra effort. A few years later, I saw that same team at an ice cream social at the office, and it didn't appear happy. The team members weren't socializing, and their body language seemed cold. When I approached them, they were complaining that there were only "chocolate Jimmies, not colored sprinkles" as a topping for the ice cream. Think about that transition: same team, same project, much different morale. It went from cheerfully working overtime, when needed, to complaining about free ice cream. How did this happen? The team had a new manager who made some bad decisions. His errors led the team down a false path and created more work for it. Senior management blamed the entire team. And when the manager took no responsibility, the team lost confidence. The project became "more work and less fun," and morale suffered. As the manager tried to improve the situation, he made things worse. He remembered that when the team members had high morale, they would occasionally go out to movies together. So, he instituted a "movie night." The team had no interest in socializing, and attendance was low. The manager began marking on performance reviews that people weren't "participating with the team." That lowered morale even more.

士气是那种你知道自己需要、但很难培养和衡量的东西。高士气团队偶尔会愉快地付出额外努力，低士气团队不会。高士气不只是关于更好的工作场所，更是关于更高产的团队。几年前，我和一个展现高士气的团队共事。有时办公室感觉更像朋友社区而不是工作场所。生产力高。我们偶尔有危机需要一点额外"推"，团队成员会自愿承担那额外努力。几年后，我在办公室冰淇淋社交会上看到同一个团队，它看起来不快乐。团队成员不社交，肢体语言看起来冷淡。当我走近他们，他们在抱怨冰淇淋浇头只有"巧克力糖针、没有彩色糖屑"。想想这个转变：同一个团队、同一个项目、士气大不同。从需要时愉快加班，变成抱怨免费冰淇淋。怎么会这样？团队来了一个新经理，做了一些糟糕决定。他的错误把团队带上错误道路、给它制造更多工作。高层管理责怪整个团队。当经理不承担责任时，团队失去信心。项目变成"更多工作、更少乐趣"，士气受损。当经理试图改善局面时，他把事情弄得更糟。他记得团队成员士气高时偶尔会一起出去看电影。于是他设立了"电影之夜"。团队对社交没兴趣，出席率低。经理开始在绩效评估里标注人们没有"参与团队"。那进一步降低了士气。

— p.192 —

In this situation, the manager had the cause and effect backward. People don't have high team morale because they socialize; they are more willing to socialize because they have high morale. As a consultant, I have tried to think about ways to measure morale. I have joked about metrics like "the ratio of cars in the parking lot at 5:05 p.m. and 4:55 p.m.," and the "number of visible Dilbert cartoons per square foot of office space." But I have realized morale isn't something to be measured, morale is the measurement. We are measuring the team's attitude. Morale is the measure of the team's confidence in its leader, confidence in its teammates, and faith in its own ability to get things done. It is your job as the software project manager to create a workplace with high morale. If team members respect you as their leader, and if they feel they can talk to you and influence the outcome of events, morale will improve. High morale results in greater satisfaction among your employees, lower turnover, and higher productivity. On top of all that, it's just nicer to be around happy people. Don't you agree?

在这种局面里，经理把因果搞反了。人们不是因为社交才有高团队士气；他们更愿意社交是因为有高士气。作为顾问，我试图想衡量士气的方法。我开过玩笑说用"下午 5:05 和 4:55 停车场车数之比"、"每平方英尺办公区可见 Dilbert 漫画数"之类指标。但我意识到士气不是要被测量的东西，士气就是测量本身。我们在测量团队的态度。士气是团队对其领导信心、对其队友信心、以及对自己完成事情能力信念的度量。作为软件项目经理，创造高士气工作场所是你的工作。如果团队成员尊重你作为领导，如果他们觉得能和你谈、能影响事件结果，士气会改善。高士气带来员工更高满意度、更低流失、更高生产力。除此之外，和快乐的人在一起就是更舒服。你不同意吗？

— p.193 —

Engage Stakeholders All Through Project Life贯穿项目全程吸引相关方

Lukeman Lawal, M.ENG, MNSE, R.ENGR. · Lekki, Lagos, NigeriaLukeman Lawal（M.ENG, MNSE, R.ENGR.）· 尼日利亚拉各斯莱基

GOOD WORKING RELATIONSHIPS with stakeholders who have significant influence on the outcomes of a project are vital. Stakeholders are individuals and groups, both inside and outside the organization, who can influence the success of the project, and/or anyone who can be affected by the project. Project managers should have a stakeholder engagement plan that includes identification of stakeholders, an assessment of their degree of influence, and an assessment of their favorability toward the project. Use this plan to deliberately build support. Engage stockholders early and keep them involved through project completion. Be sure you know the business need for the project they support. Work toward aligning the needs of all of the key stakeholders, not just the top few. It's always pertinent to find out what the key stakeholders need to become visible and vocal advocates for the project, and how the project can be made to be a win for them, as well as for your team. Once your project plan reflects the needs of the key stakeholders, insist that they demonstrate their commitment by providing the resources needed to support the project. This gives you an army of investors to fight outside stakeholders with no money or services who may want to stop the project. It is advisable to assign a single point of accountability on the project team for coordinating stakeholder management, and to interface with and actively engage key stakeholders at appropriate levels. Create and utilize a stakeholder communication plan to capture frequency of communications, content of communication, and type of delivery method. Methods and frequency of contact may differ for each stakeholder. Schedule an alignment meeting with smaller stakeholders to minimize conflicts between departments. Your stakeholder handler will follow up to ensure that critical functions/groups are represented on the core project team, or on the extended project team, as resources. Review stakeholder standards of success with decision makers at each meeting to ensure that alignment remains consistent. Here are some other suggestions: Respect the business needs of stakeholders, even if you don't agree. Ensure confidentiality on sensitive issues to build trust. Create an alliance of stakeholders to support your project. Get stakeholders actively and meaningfully involved. Solicit stakeholder ideas and use their input. Keep stakeholders informed. Leverage those with positive attitudes and get them invested—visibly if possible. However, expect setbacks and roadblocks and be ready to address them as they occur. There will always be bumps on the road, so do not put the pressure on yourself or the stakeholders to be perfect. Just deal with these issues as they arise, and learn the lessons they will teach you so you do not have to face them again. Engaging stakeholders early enough and keeping them involved as partners until the end of project will help you to avoid show stoppers. They may not understand the details of project management, but if you help them meet their business goals, they will join you in celebrating excellent project performance.

对项目结果有重大影响力的相关方，建立良好工作关系至关重要。相关方是组织内外能影响项目成功的个人和/或群体，以及任何会被项目影响的人。项目经理应有一个相关方参与计划，包括识别相关方、评估他们的影响力程度、评估他们对项目的好感度。用这个计划有意识地建立支持。尽早让相关方参与，并让他们贯穿项目完成。确保你知道他们支持的项目的业务需要。努力协调所有关键相关方的需要，不只是最上面几个。弄清关键相关方需要什么才能成为项目看得见、有声音的倡导者、以及如何让项目对他们（和你的团队）都是赢，总是切题的。一旦你的项目计划反映了关键相关方的需要，坚持让他们通过提供支持项目所需资源来展示承诺。这给你一支投资人军队，去对抗那些没出钱没出力、可能想阻止项目的外部相关方。建议在项目团队里指定一个单点负责人协调相关方管理，并在合适层级与关键相关方对接、积极吸引他们。创建并使用相关方沟通计划，记录沟通频率、沟通内容和交付方式类型。联系方式和频率对每个相关方可能不同。安排与较小相关方的对齐会议，最小化部门间冲突。你的相关方负责人会跟进，确保关键职能/群体作为代表出现在核心项目团队、或扩展项目团队作为资源。每次会议与决策者回顾相关方的成功标准，确保对齐保持一致。这里还有一些其他建议：尊重相关方的业务需要，即使你不同意；在敏感问题上确保保密以建立信任；创建相关方联盟支持你的项目；让相关方积极、有意义地参与；征求相关方想法并使用他们的输入；让相关方知情；利用态度积极的人、让他们投入——如果可能公开地。然而，预期会有挫折和路障，准备好在它们发生时应对。路上总会有颠簸，所以不要给自己或相关方施压要求完美。只是在这些问题出现时处理它们，并吸取它们教给你的教训，这样你就不必再面对它们。足够早地吸引相关方、并让他们作为伙伴参与到项目结束，会帮你避免项目拦路虎。他们可能不懂项目管理细节，但如果你帮他们达成业务目标，他们会和你一起庆祝出色的项目表现。

— p.194 —
— p.195 —

The Value of Planning规划的价值

Derry Simmel, PMP, MBA, FLMI · Chapin, South Carolina, U.S.Derry Simmel（PMP, MBA, FLMI）· 美国南卡罗来纳州查平

"In preparing for battle I have always found that plans are useless, but planning is indispensable." —Dwight D. Eisenhower, 34th President of the United States"在备战时，我总发现计划毫无用处，但规划必不可少。"——德怀特·艾森豪威尔，美国第 34 任总统

SOME PROJECT MANAGERS prefer the quote, "No plan survives contact with the enemy," by General George S. Patton. They reason that it is a waste of time to create plans, since they will be invalid almost from the beginning. This attitude has doomed many projects to failure. There will always be managers who advocate action over planning. Action is seductive, planning is boring. Boring as it may be, the sole purpose of planning is not to create a set of documents. Eisenhower realized that the discipline of planning causes you to think about your project. The planning sessions create a deeper understanding of the project. You address work, budget, resources, risks, timelines, and more. As you plan, you gain greater insight into what is needed for success. Your plans will also help you understand if, and how, goals can be achieved. Completed plans are an invaluable way to communicate about the project. Planning documents record what was discussed and decided. They do not exist to inflexibly dictate a course of action. Unfortunately, the originals will quickly lose their value and relevance. That is why we have two types of planning: initial and ongoing. The goal of initial planning is to set the course of the project. Initial planning looks at the project as a whole and considers all areas (risk, time, quality, etc.). The initial plan sets the intent of the project, and maps a reasonable course to the objectives. The course will change as more information is gained and the situation changes. This is natural. A change in the objectives is less common, and should only be done with caution.

有些项目经理更喜欢 George S. Patton 将军的那句："没有计划能在与敌人交战后存活。"他们论证说做计划是浪费时间，因为计划几乎从一开始就失效。这种态度已让许多项目注定失败。总会有经理推崇行动而非规划。行动诱人，规划无聊。尽管无聊，规划的唯一目的不是创建一套文档。艾森豪威尔意识到，规划的纪律让你思考你的项目。规划会议创造对项目更深的理解。你处理工作、预算、资源、风险、时间线等。规划时，你对成功所需获得更深洞察。你的计划还帮你理解目标能否、以及如何达成。完成的计划是沟通项目的无价方式。规划文档记录讨论了什么、决定了什么。它们不是为了僵化地规定行动路线而存在。不幸的是，原始计划会很快失去价值和相关性。这就是为什么我们有两种规划：初始和持续。初始规划的目标是设定项目路线。初始规划把项目看作整体，考虑所有领域（风险、时间、质量等）。初始计划设定项目意图，把合理路线映射到目标。路线会随更多信息获得、形势变化而改变。这是自然的。目标变更较不常见，应谨慎为之。

— p.196 —

To create an initial plan, you must think about your project, understand the risks and limitations, and build a path to success. As the project manager, you take your team through planning sessions to do this. Creating an initial level of mutual understanding is vital, particularly right after "first contact with the enemy…" reality. First contact is when the act of planning pays off. Because everyone understands the plan, each member can react independently in accordance with the intent of the plan. Knowing the overall goals and restrictions allows your team to make the right decisions quickly. This is when ongoing planning kicks in. Your ongoing planning process starts with the existing plan and modifies it to account for the new reality. You planned to start development on May 1st, but now you can't start until June 1st. How do you make up the time? Can you assign your resources to other tasks that can be done in May? Do you need more time, more money? These are your ongoing planning considerations. You plan, adjust, and then execute. Each time you plan, you are thinking and communicating about your project. These necessary and fundamental activities will never fail to yield benefits well beyond their cost.

要创建初始计划，你必须思考你的项目、理解风险和局限、建一条通往成功的路。作为项目经理，你带团队走过规划会议来做这件事。创造初始层次的相互理解至关重要，尤其在"与敌人首次接触……"现实之后。首次接触是规划行为获得回报的时候。因为每个人都理解计划，每个成员能根据计划意图独立反应。知道总体目标和限制让你的团队能快速做对决定。这就是持续规划介入的时候。你的持续规划过程从现有计划开始，修改它以适应新现实。你计划 5 月 1 日开始开发，但现在要到 6 月 1 日才能开始。你怎么补时间？你能把资源分配给 5 月能做的其他任务吗？你需要更多时间、更多钱吗？这些是你持续规划的考虑。你规划、调整、然后执行。每次规划，你都在思考和沟通你的项目。这些必要而根本的活动，永远会带来远超其成本的收益。

— p.197 —

Don't Always Be "The Messenger"别总是当「信使」

Matt Secoske · Omaha, Nebraska, U.S.Matt Secoske · 美国内布拉斯加州奥马哈

ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT ROLES of the software project manager is to facilitate an open dialogue between the various members of the team. Unfortunately, I have been on many projects where the opposite has happened. The PM became the bottleneck through which all communication flowed. He or she was "The Messenger," passing precious bits of information from one team member to the next. For a project to be organic as it progresses, information becomes the air and water feeding the code base as it grows toward fulfilling the ultimate mission of the project. All team members rely on a constant exchange of information. But if the stakeholders are forced to channel all knowledge through the PM, insurmountable problems are guaranteed. The PM, after being entrusted with current updates, may not have correctly identified all of the developers who need to receive that information. The originator of the message thinks he/she has fulfilled any obligation by passing it along to the PM. Once the communication channel oversight is discovered, the first team member may not remember exactly what she passed along earlier, as she has since moved on to newer challenges. The PM, overwhelmed with technological reports he or she may not understand, quickly becomes incapable of being the single point of conductivity for project wisdom. There is an even more damaging role than The Messenger, in which a well-meaning but clueless PM becomes "The Scrambler." As a project grows, so does the amount of nontechnical information needed to keep it running smoothly. Developers need to know the business rules, the business champion needs to know the status of the deliverables, and various other people need insight into where the project stands in relation to its schedule, cost, and quality metrics. As this amount of information grows, so does the likelihood that a non-omnipotent PM will miscommunicate. The Scrambler has struck! For example, a business rule that appears to have little impact on the project on the surface may in fact be a major roadblock once its true intent is discovered. Sizable changes to the code base may need to be done in order to repair the damages. A project manager needs to get the right stakeholders together to talk about the right topic at the right time. Finding a time to have people from disparate departments available to meet may seem daunting. The practice? The PM, trying to solve a scheduling issue says, "Cheri, I'll take this directly to Bob, and get back to you with the answer." This can work for short, nontechnical questions. But, be aware that success in small ventures can insidiously evolve you into a Messenger or a Scrambler. Invariably something is missed in the translation, leading to excessive wasted time spent trying to sort out the repercussions. Providing clear, open channels for communication, along with archiving discussions and decisions, allows all team members to interact directly with one another. This keeps The Messenger and The Scrambler project manager at bay, and keeps the software project moving forward.

软件项目经理最重要的角色之一，是促进团队各成员间的开放对话。不幸的是，我在许多项目上看到相反的情况。项目经理成了所有沟通流过的瓶颈。他/她是"信使"，把宝贵的信息一点一点从一个团队成员传给下一个。项目要随进展有机生长，信息就成为滋养代码库的空气和水，代码库向实现项目终极使命生长。所有团队成员依赖持续的信息交换。但如果相关方被迫把所有知识都通过项目经理传递，不可逾越的问题就在所难免。项目经理被托付了最新更新后，可能没有正确识别所有需要接收该信息的开发。消息发出者以为自己把它传给项目经理就尽了义务。一旦沟通渠道疏漏被发现，第一个团队成员可能记不清她之前传了什么，因为她已转向更新的挑战。项目经理被他/她可能不懂的技术报告淹没，很快变得无法作为项目智慧的单一传导点。还有一个比信使更具破坏性的角色：一个好心但摸不着头脑的项目经理变成"搅混者"。随项目增长，让它顺畅运行所需的非技术信息量也增长。开发需要知道业务规则，业务倡导者需要知道交付物状态，其他各种人需要洞察项目相对进度、成本和质量指标的位置。随信息量增长，一个非全能项目经理传达错误信息的可能性也增长。搅混者出手了！例如，一条表面上对项目影响不大的业务规则，一旦发现真实意图，可能实际上是重大路障。可能需要对代码库做相当大的变更来修复损害。项目经理需要在正确时间把正确相关方聚在一起讨论正确话题。找一个让不同部门的人都能开会的时间可能令人生畏。常见做法？项目经理为解决一个排期问题说："Cheri，我直接拿这个去找 Bob，然后带答案回来给你。"这对简短、非技术问题可能奏效。但是，要意识到小事上的成功会潜移默化地把你变成信使或搅混者。翻译中总会漏掉什么，导致浪费过多时间去理清后果。提供清晰、开放的沟通渠道，加上归档讨论和决定，让所有团队成员直接互动。这把信使和搅混者项目经理挡在外面，让软件项目向前推进。

— p.198 —
— p.199 —

Effectively Manage the Deliverables有效管理交付物

Ernani Marques da Silva, MBA, PMP, PgMP · Mairipora, Sao Paulo, BrazilErnani Marques da Silva（MBA, PMP, PgMP）· 巴西圣保罗马伊里波朗

PROJECTS ARE COMPRISED OF A SET OF DELIVERABLES that, when completed, constitute the completion of the whole product, service, or result. For software development projects, integrating all of the components is crucial for the final result to work properly. The components, of course, vary depending on the kind of software you are building. So, the deliverables are the major components that should actively be planned, controlled, monitored, and managed by following these tips: Identify the deliverables. Identified deliverables outline the full solution, identify the order in which they should be created and delivered, identify metrics that should be used to monitor and control their development and delivery, and actively monitor their progress against the planned baseline and metrics defined. It is very important to break deliverables into partial packets of code, each created to provide a special software function. This is especially important for complex projects/environments and projects developed by third parties. Do not wait to receive the full work package at the end. It is a good practice to arrange for the delivery of project parts bit by bit, and follow a preplanned process to deploy them to other members of the software team for use in their own development work. Monitor and control the deliverables. Once you have defined the means by which the work packages (functional code bits) will be built, monitored, and controlled, you must actively monitor and control the building phase to check whether the work is being done as planned. Checkpoints, metrics, and key performance indicators (KPIs) should be shared with all project team members. At the checkpoints, the KPIs and metrics should be evaluated against the baseline and trend analysis in order to identify variances. This way, corrective action can be done based on actual metrics, rather than hunches or hearsay. Manage the deliverables. Once the anticipated work is delivered, the code should be tested and deployed to a small group of users in order to verify that it complies with requirements before it can be considered finished. This approach helps identify problems so that corrective action can be taken before the software is deployed to the entire user group. Throughout this approach, it is very important to remember that all mini-deliverables will be ready in phases and they should be tested in an integrated fashion (like a wave). If you wait until the full code set is delivered, you could receive a body of code with a lot of unknown errors/defects or unexpected behavior. Because the product/service/result was built with these issues, their effect is both buried and multiplied. The cost and the time spent in order to fix all nonworking code at this point can be very high. You can balance and examine the vendor's experience in your company's environment, and in the system, against the complexity required by development and decide whether this approach should be good for you or not. In general, it is most useful for complex solutions or for new technology/new solutions.

项目由一组交付物构成，它们完成后即构成整个产品、服务或结果的完成。对软件开发项目，集成所有组件对最终结果正常工作至关重要。组件当然因你在造的软件种类而异。因此，交付物是主要组件，应积极规划、控制、监控和管理，遵循以下提示：识别交付物。识别出的交付物勾勒完整方案，识别它们应被创建和交付的顺序，识别应用于监控和控制其开发与交付的指标，并对照计划基线和定义指标积极监控其进展。把交付物拆成部分代码包（每个为提供一个特殊软件功能而创建）非常重要。这对复杂项目/环境和第三方开发的项目尤其重要。不要等到最后才收到完整工作包。安排项目部分一点一点交付、并按预设计划把它们部署给软件团队其他成员用于自己的开发工作，是好实践。监控和控制交付物。一旦你定义了工作包（功能代码片段）将如何被构建、监控和控制，你必须积极监控和控制构建阶段，检查工作是否按计划进行。检查点、指标和关键绩效指标（KPI）应与所有项目团队成员共享。在检查点，KPI 和指标应对照基线和趋势分析评估，以识别偏差。这样，纠正行动可基于实际指标而非直觉或传闻。管理交付物。一旦预期工作交付，代码应被测试并部署给一小群用户，以验证它符合需求后才能算完成。这种方法帮助识别问题，以便在软件部署给整个用户群前采取纠正行动。贯穿这种方法，非常重要的是记住所有小交付物会分阶段就绪，它们应以集成方式（像波浪）测试。如果你等到完整代码集交付，你可能收到一大堆带大量未知错误/缺陷或意外行为的代码。因为产品/服务/结果是带着这些问题构建的，它们的影响既被掩埋又被放大。此时修复所有不工作代码的成本和时间可能非常高。你可以权衡、考察供应商在你公司环境和系统中的经验，对照开发所需复杂度，决定这种方法是否适合你。一般来说，它对复杂方案或新技术/新方案最有用。

— p.200 —
— p.201 —

We Are Project Managers, Not Superheroes我们是项目经理，不是超级英雄

Angyne J. Schock-Smith, PMP · Phillipsburg, New Jersey, U.S.Angyne J. Schock-Smith（PMP）· 美国新泽西州菲利普斯堡

THIS IS A TIP THAT IS USEFUL if you're a software project manager in information technology environments, but is also transferrable to whatever type of projects you manage. "We are project managers, not superheroes," is part of my introductory routine when I deliver training on project management skills. When talking about the characteristics of a good project manager, my favorite line is, "Get out your capes, people! It takes a superhero to do all a software project manager must do, and to do it well." However, since this comes early in the training, I have to offer some hope. So I say, "OK, some of us mere mortals actually become good project managers. What's the trick?" I believe this trick has three parts: Know your personal strengths and weaknesses. Know the personal strengths and weaknesses of your team. Use this knowledge to create complementary partnerships with team members who possess strengths where you have gaps. How can you get to know your personal strengths and weaknesses? Get out your copies of all the old personality or work behavior tests you've ever taken. Be honest as you extrapolate data from these old evaluations. Were you honest when you took the questionnaire? Does the "label" still fit, or have you grown and changed since that time? Which of the label's associated strengths and weaknesses most accurately describe you right now? Don't try to figure out which label would make the best project manager. There is no right answer to that question. A good project manager has to be flexible, i.e., be able to diagnose each situation and shift out of his/her comfort zone to respond in the most effective way. From your available data, create a fresh, current personal inventory of strengths and weaknesses. Keep it where you will always be able to find it and update it as you continue to learn more about yourself. After that, the rest is downhill! Use an available strengths inventory to assess your team. Then, look for people on the team who have strengths in the areas listed on your personal weakness inventory. For me (an Expressive type, if you know the Social Styles types), my weakness is attention to detail. I'll always need someone (an Analytical type) to keep me on track in that area! If you're likely to try to please others more than you should, you may need someone to help you drive the project forward more forcefully than you would be comfortable doing yourself. Make sure that you have teammates with complementary skills working with you in areas where your weaknesses lie. But you don't have to tell them that's what you are doing, right? Keep some mystique about it, and maybe you can convince the team that you are a superhero. I won't tell anyone otherwise.

这是一条在 IT 环境做软件项目经理时有用的提示，但也可迁移到你管理的任何类型项目。"我们是项目经理，不是超级英雄"是我讲项目管理技能培训时开场白的一部分。谈到好项目经理的特征时，我最喜欢的一句话是："拿出你们的斗篷吧各位！要把软件项目经理必须做的一切都做好，需要一个超级英雄。"然而，因为这是培训开头，我必须给点希望。于是我说："好吧，我们有些凡人真的成了好项目经理。诀窍是什么？"我相信诀窍有三部分：知道你个人的长处和弱点；知道你团队成员个人的长处和弱点；用这些知识与在你短板处有长处的团队成员建立互补伙伴关系。你怎么了解自己的长处和弱点？拿出你做过的所有旧人格或工作行为测试的副本。从这些旧评估外推数据时要诚实。你做问卷时诚实吗？那个"标签"还合身吗，还是从那时起你成长和改变了？标签相关的哪些长处和弱点最准确地描述现在的你？别试图弄清楚哪个标签能造就最好的项目经理。这个问题没有正确答案。好项目经理必须灵活，即能诊断每种情况、走出他/她的舒适区以最有效方式回应。从你可用数据，创建一份新鲜、当前的个人长处和弱点清单。放在你总能找到的地方，随你继续了解自己而更新。之后就是下坡路了！用一份可用的长处清单评估你的团队。然后，在团队里找那些在你个人弱点清单所列领域有长处的人。对我（一个表达型，如果你知道社会风格类型），我的弱点是对细节的关注。我总需要一个人（分析型）在那个领域让我不跑偏！如果你可能比应该的更想讨好别人，你可能需要一个人帮你把项目比你自己舒服的方式更有力地往前推。确保在你弱点所在的领域有互补技能的队友和你共事。但你不必告诉他们你在这么做，对吧？保持一点神秘感，也许你能让团队相信你是超级英雄。我不会告诉别人真相。

— p.202 —
— p.203 —

Increase Communication: Hold Frequent, Instant Meetings增加沟通：开频繁的即时会议

Richard Sheridan · Ann Arbor, Michigan, U.S.Richard Sheridan · 美国密歇根州安娜堡

SOFTWARE PROJECT MANAGERS often fall into the deadly trap of regularly scheduling their teams for painful meetings that have the unfortunate, unintended effect of actually decreasing communications. One of the all-time dreaded meetings is the classic Monday morning status meeting. As if Mondays weren't bad enough already! If you aren't convinced that most meetings should be killed, try this experiment. As the software project manager, don't show up. Ask one of your trusted colleagues about the meeting you skipped. Did they hold it without you? If the meeting only happens when the boss or project manager shows up, kill it. Your team is telling you they don't get value out of it. Never hold meetings where only one person gets value. At my organization, we do everything we can to eliminate unproductive meetings and replace them with simpler communication paths among team members. For example, we have the team work all day, every day, in one big open room with no walls, offices, cubes, or doors. Thus, when I need an answer from someone, I can simply say, "Hey, James." In less than 30 seconds, James and I have exchanged the necessary information and can get back to work without actually moving (or sending emails back and forth). Imagine an all-company meeting with 60 people that is as easy to set up as shouting out "Hey, everybody!" Everyone stops what they are doing and responds, "Hey, Rich!" The meeting can take a few, short minutes and then everyone turns back to work without moving from his/her seat. Our rituals and ceremonies include weekly "Show and Tells" to demonstrate progress on projects to sponsors, weekly "planning games" to authorize project scope, daily stand-up meetings, and weekly kick-off meetings to brainstorm about how we will work together toward common goals on client projects in the upcoming week. The meeting has a structure that makes participation easy and fun. Try a daily stand-up meeting for one week and see if it catches on. Here are some lessons we've learned to make this meeting more effective: Invite everyone involved in the project. We often have 50-60 people in this meeting. Call the meeting with an alarm clock loud enough for everyone to hear. An impartial device calling the meeting is more likely to get participation. We use a dartboard that has an alarm clock in it. Use a speaking token. We use a plastic Viking helmet to control the meeting. Just hand it around the circle of people standing (no sitting allowed). The person who has the token has the floor. Have people report what they recently completed, what they are working on, and where they need help. Help doesn't come during the meeting, but afterward. Our typical stand-up meeting takes 13 minutes! Call it, assemble it, hold it, give everyone a chance to talk, finish it, and get back to work in 13 minutes. I defy most organizations to complete a useful meeting of 60 people in 13 minutes.

软件项目经理常常掉进一个致命陷阱：定期给团队排痛苦的会议，这些会议有一个不幸的、非预期的效果——实际上减少了沟通。有史以来最可怕的会议之一是经典的周一早晨状态会。好像周一还不够糟似的！如果你还不信大多数会议该被砍掉，试试这个实验。作为软件项目经理，你别出现。问你一个信任的同事你跳过的会怎么样了。他们没你也开了吗？如果会议只在老板或项目经理出现时才开，砍掉它。你的团队在告诉你他们从中得不到价值。永远不要开只有一个人得到价值的会。在我的组织，我们尽一切可能消除非生产性会议，用团队成员间更简单的沟通路径替代它们。例如，我们让团队整天、每天在一个大开放房间里工作，没有墙、办公室、隔间或门。因此，当我需要某人答案时，我可以简单说："嘿，James。"不到 30 秒，James 和我就交换了必要信息，可以回去工作，根本不用动地方（或来回发邮件）。想象一个 60 人的全公司会议，召集起来像喊一声"嘿，各位！"一样容易。每个人停下手里的事回应："嘿，Rich！"会议可以只花短短几分钟，然后每个人不离开座位就回去工作。我们的仪式包括每周"展示讲述"向发起人演示项目进展、每周"规划游戏"批准项目范围、每日站会、以及每周启动会来头脑风暴下一周我们如何在客户项目上共同朝目标努力。会议有让参与轻松有趣的结构。试一周每日站会，看看能不能流行起来。这里是我们学到的让这个会议更有效的经验：邀请项目涉及的每个人。我们这个会常有 50-60 人。用一个足够响、每个人都能听到的闹钟召集会议。一个中立设备召集会议更可能得到参与。我们用一个里面有闹钟的飞镖靶。使用发言令牌。我们用一个塑料维京头盔控制会议。就在站成一圈的人之间传（不许坐）。拿令牌的人发言。让人们报告最近完成了什么、在做什么、哪里需要帮助。帮助不在会议期间来，在会后。我们典型的站会花 13 分钟！召集、集合、开、给每个人说话机会、结束、13 分钟内回去工作。我敢说大多数组织没法在 13 分钟内完成一个 60 人的有用会议。

— p.204 —
— p.205 —

Flexibility Simplifies Project Management灵活性简化项目管理

Krishna Kadali, M. Tech · Kondapur, Hyderabad, IndiaKrishna Kadali（M. Tech）· 印度海得拉巴孔达普尔

MIYAMOTO MUSASHI, A FAMOUS 17TH-CENTURY SAMURAI, believed in the principle, "Do not develop an attachment to any one weapon or any one school of fighting." This advice also rings true in our project life. It is imperative that we not get too attached to any one management principle, software tool, or programming language as our only weapon. It is only through seeing our resources in a flexible way, arrangeable in many varying configurations, that we are able to prepare the best response to the customer problems that become our project. Take an open-minded approach right from the beginning when you define your project requirements. If you already have your weapon and fight plan chosen before you talk to the customer, how can you be sure your solution is the best one? Before picking your weapon, examine all your customer's requirements. What problem is the customer trying to solve using your new software? The problems are usually attached to some business logic showing that the current resources aren't feature- or function-rich enough. Next, consider the pool of existing factors and systems within your organization. Reusing parts of existing environmental systems skillfully can shorten and ease your project path. Available enterprise environment factors include such diverse things as the company infrastructure of existing facilities, equipment and software, commercial and private databases, programming tools, and human resource skills. A resource-oriented analysis of the customer requirements to be met by the software or other project deliverables will reveal some of these underlying resources that already exist in the organization: "Our users must be able to see the XPP34 call center system side by side with our corporate accounts receivable system. Your product will need to be merged, or be compatible, with our 4465IL legacy software.

17 世纪著名武士宫本武藏信奉一条原则："不要执着于任何一种武器或任何一派格斗术。"这条建议在我们的项目生活中也成立。我们绝不能过于执着于某一种管理原则、软件工具或编程语言作为唯一武器。只有以灵活方式看待我们的资源——可按多种配置排列——我们才能为成为我们项目的客户问题准备最佳回应。从定义项目需求一开始就采取开放心态。如果你在和客户谈之前就已经选好武器和作战计划，你怎么能确定你的方案是最好的？选武器之前，考察客户的所有需求。客户想用你的新软件解决什么问题？这些问题通常附在某些业务逻辑上，显示当前资源在功能上不够丰富。接下来，考虑你组织内现有因素和系统的池子。巧妙复用现有环境系统的部分，可以缩短和缓解你的项目路径。可用企业环境因素包括如此多样的东西：现有设施的公司基础设施、设备和软件、商业和私有数据库、编程工具、人力资源技能。对软件或其他项目交付物要满足的客户需求做资源导向分析，会揭示组织中已存在的一些底层资源："我们用户必须能并排看到 XPP34 呼叫中心系统和公司应收账款系统。你的产品需要与我们的 4465IL 遗留软件合并或兼容。

— p.206 —

Your job is to ask the right questions about various final performance results expected by the customer, and about how existing resources/software/systems and your new code output are to interrelate. You may be able to lay a foundation for changes your customer will want in the future using this resource-oriented approach. At the end of this analysis, your software begins to take shape as a set of new resources—things that not only solve today's problems, but that can be used to complete future projects and interact with future software. Once you know what the customer wants and what resources are already available within your organization, now you can choose your best weapon to fight the problem. Actual development can first focus on a few key requirements you deliver to gain the customer's confidence. The modules and services needed for satisfying the key requirements should be implemented first. Leaving your mind open to new paths for software design provides a pleasant way to handle software projects in the world of constantly changing requirements. This flexibility will simplify your project management challenges, and creating fresh weapons and plans keeps your workday interesting and enriching.

你的工作是就客户期望的各种最终性能结果、以及现有资源/软件/系统与你的新代码输出将如何相互关联，提出正确问题。用这种资源导向方法，你也许能为客户未来想要的变更打下基础。分析结束时，你的软件开始成形为一组新资源——不仅解决今天问题、还能用来完成未来项目、与未来软件交互的东西。一旦你知道客户要什么、你组织内已有什么资源，现在你可以选最佳武器来打这个问题了。实际开发可以先聚焦于你交付的几个关键需求以赢得客户信心。满足关键需求所需的模块和服务应先实现。对软件设计的新路径保持开放心态，为在需求不断变化的世界里处理软件项目提供了一种愉快方式。这种灵活性会简化你的项目管理挑战，而创造新鲜武器和计划让你的工作日有趣而充实。
